documentation: Every corvidae workspace's disposition when the mirror transform emits a public target, plus a ruling on each name that is published (or was once reserved) without corvidae source. The transform hard-errors on any workspace absent from `workspaces`; it never silently skips one. `publish-as` carries the public npm name, and is the only disposition that puts anything on the registry. `private-workspace` ships to the mirror repository but never into a tarball. `exclude` is not emitted at all. Names under `publishedOnly` have no corvidae source, so no sync can maintain them: `keep` means a human maintains it elsewhere, `deprecate` means publish a deprecation notice, and `orphan-untouched` means leave the registry entry exactly as it is.

@lostgradient/evaluation.reason: Never published and new in this repository (COR-1348). It scores completed Operative runs against versioned evaluator configurations, nothing imports it yet, and no workspace the mirror emits depends on it. `private-workspace` would ship its source to a public repository, making a brand-new package public for the first time as a side effect of an internal feature; `exclude` keeps that a deliberate decision. Reversible: promote to `private-workspace` or `publish-as` when a public consumer exists.

@lostgradient/weft.name: @lostgradient/weft
@lostgradient/weft.reason: Already published under this name. Ships standalone from stevekinney/weft.

@lostgradient/weft-ui.reason: The repository owner ruled 2026-09-23 (COR-1196) that weft-ui ships to the cinder mirror as unpublished source rather than as a published package. `scripts/mirror/package-surface.json` recorded a surface for an old `dist/mount.js` bundle whose build scripts corvidae does not carry, while corvidae's source (`components/weft-ui/src/index.ts`) now exports a `WeftConsole` Svelte component — the recorded surface described a package that no longer exists. `npm view @lostgradient/weft-ui` still returns 404 and COR-1194 records its trusted-publisher registration as never completed, so this ruling changes nothing on the registry. A separate issue is to design its public API before any publish; the `@lostgradient/weft-ui` name stays available for that publish.

@lostgradient/operative.reason: Published from the agent-bureau mirror until the repository owner ruled on 2026-10-14 that only Weft and Cinder's packages publish from now on, which retired the agent-bureau target. The registry keeps @lostgradient/operative@0.17.0, the last release; no sync maintains it any more. `exclude` rather than `private-workspace` because no remaining target carries it. Deprecating the registry entry and archiving stevekinney/agent-bureau are the owner's to do, outside this pipeline.

@lostgradient/chat.reason: Published from the cinder mirror until the repository owner ruled on 2026-10-14 to stop publishing it. The registry keeps @lostgradient/chat@0.16.0, the last release. `target-owned.json` retires the cinder mirror's `packages/chat` copy so that the mirror stops releasing it.

@lostgradient/testing.reason: Test infrastructure imported from 505 test files and 26 non-test files, all of which are harnesses, fixture loaders, and scripts. Never in a runtime dependencies edge. @lostgradient/playground.reason: The playground application moved into corvidae in COR-1200, and COR-1201 moved the cinder.website deployment onto it, building from `applications/playground` in this repository. The public stevekinney/cinder repository's former copy at `packages/playground` was deleted in that repository's own pull request (cinder#1602), because the same change had to remove the copy's references from Cinder-owned release tooling that the transform cannot write; `target-owned.json`'s `retired` list names the directory and its deployment workflow so that a restored copy is removed by the next sync. The entry stays `exclude` because the application is private to corvidae and hosts a deployment, not a published package.

@lostgradient/terminal.reason: New in COR-482 and never published. Excluded from the mirror by the repository owner's ruling of 2026-09-25 (not published until a later publication project). It is the browser terminal component and controller, and it imports only the platform-neutral root export of `@lostgradient/ventriloquist`. It depends on published workspaces (cinder) but nothing the mirror emits depends on it. Reversible: promote to `private-workspace` or `publish-as` when the later publication project rules on a public home.

@lostgradient/ventriloquist.reason: New in COR-482 and never published. Excluded from the mirror by the repository owner's ruling of 2026-09-25 (not published until a later publication project). It is the terminal wire protocol and session core with Bun pipe, PTY, and WebSocket host helpers behind `./bun` and `./websocket`. Its only consumer is `@lostgradient/terminal`, which is itself excluded, so nothing the mirror emits depends on it. Reversible: promote to `private-workspace` or `publish-as` when the later publication project rules on a public home.
